stories.headline: Amazon Invests Up to $25B in Anthropic, Secures $100B+ AWS Compute Commitment Over 10 Years

key_facts.fact: Amazon will invest $5 billion in Anthropic immediately, with up to $20 billion more tied to commercial milestones, on top of $8 billion already invested — bringing total potential investment to ~$33 billion.

Anthropic commits to spending more than $100 billion on AWS technologies over the next 10 years, including current and future generations of Trainium chips (Trainium2 through Trainium4) and tens of millions of Graviton CPU cores.
Anthropic secures up to 5 gigawatts of compute capacity, with nearly 1 GW of combined Trainium2 and Trainium3 capacity expected online by end of 2026.
Anthropic's annualized revenue has reached $30 billion, up from approximately $9 billion at end of 2025.
The initial investment is priced at Anthropic's latest valuation of $380 billion. Over 100,000 customers run Claude models on AWS.
The deal follows Amazon's $50 billion investment in OpenAI announced two months earlier, making Amazon the largest investor in both leading AI labs.

stories.headline: Amazon Invests Up to $25B in Anthropic; Anthropic Commits $100B+ on AWS for 5GW of Trainium

key_facts.fact: Amazon will invest $5 billion in Anthropic immediately, with up to $20 billion more tied to commercial milestones, bringing total potential investment to $33 billion on top of $8 billion already invested since 2023.
Anthropic committed to spending more than $100 billion over the next 10 years on AWS technologies, securing up to 5 gigawatts of compute capacity across Trainium2, Trainium3, and Trainium4 chips.
Nearly 1 gigawatt of Trainium2 and Trainium3 capacity is expected to come online by end of 2026; Anthropic already uses over 1 million Trainium2 chips through Project Rainier.
Anthropic's run-rate revenue has hit $30 billion, up from roughly $9 billion at end of 2025, with over 100,000 customers running Claude on Amazon Bedrock.
Combined with a separate Google/Broadcom deal for 4.5GW of TPU capacity, Anthropic now has commitments for nearly 10GW of AI compute across two major cloud platforms.

stories.headline: Apple Names Johny Srouji Chief Hardware Officer, Reorganizes Hardware Into Five Groups

key_facts.fact: Apple promoted Johny Srouji to the newly created role of Chief Hardware Officer, effective April 20, combining hardware engineering and hardware technologies divisions under one organization.

Srouji organized the combined division into five areas: hardware engineering (Tom Marieb, ex-Intel), silicon (Sri Santhanam, 18-year veteran), advanced technologies (Zongjian Chen), platform architecture (Tim Millet, 21-year veteran), and program management (Donny Nordhues).
The restructuring accompanies the announcement that John Ternus will succeed Tim Cook as Apple CEO on September 1, with Cook becoming executive chairman.
Srouji joined Apple in 2008 to lead development of the A4, Apple's first custom system-on-a-chip, after senior positions at Intel and IBM in processor design.

The reorganization returns Apple to an earlier model used under former hardware chief Bob Mansfield, when hardware operated as a single unit; it was later split, allowing Ternus and Srouji to rise through separate divisions.

stories.headline: Bezos' Project Prometheus Nears $10B Fundraise at $38B Valuation for Industrial AI

key_facts.fact: Jeff Bezos' AI startup Project Prometheus is close to finalizing a $10 billion funding round at a $38 billion post-money valuation, according to the Financial Times.
JPMorgan and BlackRock are among the investors in the new round. The startup was initially set up with $6.2 billion in funding, sourced in part from Bezos himself.

Project Prometheus, co-founded by Bezos and scientist Vik Bajaj, focuses on AI models for the physical world — accelerating engineering and manufacturing in aerospace, automobiles, and semiconductors.
The startup has recruited dozens of employees from leading AI labs including OpenAI and Google DeepMind, in San Francisco, Zurich, and London.

stories.headline: BMW Expands Humanoid Robot Program to German EV Factory After Building 30K+ Vehicles in US Pilot

key_facts.fact: BMW is deploying Hexagon Robotics' AEON humanoid robots at its Leipzig, Germany factory for EV production, after a successful pilot at its Spartanburg, South Carolina plant.
BMW's earlier pilot used Figure 02 humanoid robots for precise sheet metal positioning on the X3 production line, contributing to building more than 30,000 vehicles.
The AEON robots use AI-based motion control and real-time sensors to adapt to their environment without constant human direction, which Hexagon calls 'Physical AI.'
BMW executive Michael Nikolaides framed the deployment as part of the company's broader iFACTORY initiative for digitalization and production competitiveness.

stories.headline: CFIUS Blocks Chinese LED Maker Sanan's $239M Acquisition of Dutch Firm Lumileds

key_facts.fact: China's leading LED chipmaker Sanan Optoelectronics and its Malaysian partner withdrew their US$239 million all-cash offer to acquire Lumileds Holding after CFIUS concluded the deal posed 'irresolvable U.S. national security risks.'
No equity transfer payment had been made and the target shares had not been delivered; Sanan said the termination will not materially affect its operations or financial position.
Lumileds ranks third globally in automotive lighting LED revenue behind ams OSRAM and Nichia, and is part of Apple's smartphone flash LED supply chain.
Sanan had planned to use Lumileds' manufacturing facilities in Singapore and Malaysia to strengthen its overseas production capacity and global customer supply.

stories.headline: Renewables Overtake Coal in Global Power Generation for First Time in Over a Century

key_facts.fact: Clean electricity met all growth in global power demand in 2025 (887 TWh vs 849 TWh demand growth), keeping fossil fuel generation flat for the first time this century, per Ember's Global Electricity Review 2026.
Renewables reached nearly 34% of global electricity generation, overtaking coal's 33% share for the first time in over a century; coal power dropped by 63 TWh (-0.6%).
Solar generation rose 30% in 2025 (636 TWh increase), the fastest growth rate in eight years; solar alone met 75% of global electricity demand growth, while solar and wind together met 99%.
Battery storage grew 46% in 2025 as costs fell 45%; enough capacity was added to shift 14% of solar generation to times when the sun isn't shining.
Global emissions intensity fell to 458 gCO2e per kWh in 2025, down 2.7% from 2024 and down 16% from 2005.

stories.headline: EU to Unblock €90B Ukraine Loan on Wednesday as Orbán Lifts Blockade

key_facts.fact: EU countries will on Wednesday unblock a €90 billion loan to Ukraine, approved in December to cover Kyiv's military and financial needs through 2027, after outgoing Hungarian PM Viktor Orbán lifted his blockade.
The blockade was removed after April 12 Hungarian elections ended Orbán's 16-year rule; incoming PM Péter Magyar promised smoother EU relations and criticized Orbán for bowing to Russian influence.
Ukraine will resume transit of Russian oil to Hungary via the Druzhba pipeline on April 21 at noon as part of the deal; deliveries had been stopped since January 21.
French President Macron said with Orbán's departure, 'we can be reasonably optimistic about the sound progress and implementation' of the EU loan.
Germany summoned the Russian Ambassador on Monday over 'direct threats from Russia' against targets in Germany; Russia's Defense Ministry had named three German firms supplying drones to Ukraine.

stories.headline: FDA Accepts Roche's Gazyva Filing for Lupus, Potential First Anti-CD20 Therapy for SLE

key_facts.fact: The FDA accepted Roche's supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for Gazyva/Gazyvaro (obinutuzumab) for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); a decision is expected by December 2026.
If approved, Gazyva would be the first anti-CD20 therapy to directly target B cells in SLE, potentially becoming the new standard of care for a disease affecting more than 3 million people worldwide.

Phase III ALLEGORY results showed 76.7% of patients on Gazyva plus standard therapy achieved SRI-4 response at 52 weeks vs 53.5% on placebo (adjusted difference 23.1%, p<0.001); the remission rate more than doubled (33.8% vs 13.8%).

Gazyva-treated patients were significantly less likely to have disease flares through 52 weeks (HR 0.58, p=0.002) and had lower steroid dependence, with the glucocorticoid dose sustained at ≤7.5 mg/day from week 40 to 52.

stories.headline: GitHub Copilot Pauses New Signups, Tightens Limits, and Removes Opus Models From Pro Tier

key_facts.fact: GitHub paused new sign-ups for Copilot Pro, Pro+, and Student plans on April 20, citing agentic workflows that 'fundamentally changed Copilot's compute demands.'
Opus models removed from Pro plans entirely; Opus 4.7 remains available on Pro+ only. Opus 4.5 and 4.6 being removed from Pro+ as previously announced.
Usage limits tightened for individual plans, with Pro+ now offering more than 5× the limits of Pro. Two types of limits: session limits (prevent peak overload) and weekly token-consumption caps.
GitHub is offering refunds for Pro or Pro+ subscriptions canceled between April 20 and May 20, 2026, acknowledging the changes are disruptive.
Long-running, parallelized agentic sessions now consume far more resources than the original plan structure was built to support, GitHub VP of product Joe Binder said.

stories.headline: Google's Sergey Brin Forms DeepMind 'Coding Strike Team' to Close Gap With Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Google co-founder Sergey Brin is personally leading a new DeepMind 'Coding Strike Team' aimed at closing Gemini's gap with Anthropic's Claude on code generation, according to The Information.

In an internal memo, Brin wrote: 'To win the final sprint, we must urgently bridge the gap in agentic execution and turn our models into primary developers.' He framed improving coding as the path to self-improving AI — AI that trains the next AI.
The strike team is led by research engineer Sebastian Borgeaud, who previously ran DeepMind's pretraining. Both Brin and DeepMind CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu are directly involved.

DeepMind researchers internally rate Claude's code-writing above Gemini's, which drove Brin's push. Google is now training models on its own proprietary codebase rather than public datasets typically used for general-purpose coding agents.
Gemini engineers are now required to use Google's internal agent tools on complex tasks, with usage tracked on a company leaderboard called 'Jetski.'

stories.headline: Humble Unveils Fully Electric Cabless Autonomous Truck, Exits Stealth With $24M Seed

key_facts.fact: Humble unveiled the Humble Hauler, a fully electric cabless autonomous truck designed for the U.S. freight industry, coming out of stealth mode.
The company raised a $24 million seed round led by Eclipse Ventures.
The cabless design eliminates the driver cabin entirely, targeting the $900 billion U.S. freight industry with a purpose-built autonomous-first form factor.

stories.headline: Iran-US Ceasefire Expires Wednesday as Both Sides Signal Round 2 Talks in Islamabad

key_facts.fact: The two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran is set to expire Wednesday evening Washington time; Trump told CNBC it is 'highly unlikely' he would extend it without a deal.

Two regional officials told the AP that the US and Iran are signaling they will hold a new round of ceasefire talks in Islamabad, with VP JD Vance and Iran's Qalibaf expected to arrive early Wednesday.
Iran's chief negotiator Qalibaf warned that Iran 'will not accept negotiations under the shadow of threats' and has prepared 'new cards on the battlefield' if the ceasefire ends.
Since the war started on Feb 28, fighting has killed at least 3,375 people in Iran, more than 2,290 in Lebanon, 23 in Israel, and 13 US service members.
Only 12 vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours as traffic through the chokepoint remains severely disrupted; up to 10 million barrels per day of crude remain shut in.
Kuwait declared force majeure on shipments of crude oil and refined products after the blockade prevented vessels from entering the Persian Gulf.
Brent crude slipped 0.4% to $95.09/barrel on Tuesday as markets bet talks would resume, pulling back after a $5+/barrel surge the previous session.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI Releases Kimi K2.6, Open-Weight 1T-Parameter Model Rivaling Frontier Labs on Coding

key_facts.fact: Kimi K2.6 is a 1 trillion total parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 32 billion active parameters per token, 384 experts (8 routed + 1 shared), 256K context window, and native multimodal input (text, image, video).
K2.6 scores 80.2% on SWE-Bench Verified, 58.6% on SWE-Bench Pro (beating Claude Opus 4.6's 53.4% and GPT-5.4's 57.7%), and 54.0% on Humanity's Last Exam with tools (beating GPT-5.4's 52.1%).
The model supports an agent-swarm primitive coordinating up to 300 parallel sub-agents across 4,000 steps per run, and can code continuously for 12+ hours.
K2.6 ranks #4 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0, scoring 54 — just 3 points behind Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4, all tied at 57.
API pricing is $0.60 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens — roughly 10× cheaper than Claude Opus 4.7. Weights available on Hugging Face under Modified MIT License.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Chronicle for Codex, Building AI Memory From Screen Captures

key_facts.fact: Chronicle is a research preview feature in Codex for macOS that periodically captures screenshots, sends them to OpenAI servers for processing, and stores text summaries as local unencrypted Markdown files to build persistent context.
Available only to ChatGPT Pro subscribers ($100+/month) on Apple Silicon Macs. Not available in the EU, UK, or Switzerland. Requires macOS Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions.
Screen captures are stored temporarily on-device and auto-deleted after 6 hours. OpenAI says screenshots are not stored on servers after processing and are not used for training.

Chronicle processes screenshots in the cloud, contrasting with Microsoft Recall's on-device approach and drawing comparisons to the now-defunct Rewind AI. OpenAI warns the feature increases risk of prompt injection from screen content.

Over one million developers have used Codex, and usage doubled following the GPT-5.2-Codex model launch in December. Chronicle is part of a broader update that added computer use, in-app browser, image generation, and 90+ plugins.

stories.headline: US Space Force Cancels GPS Ground Control System After 16 Years and Nearly $8B

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon canceled the GPS Next-Generation Operational Control System (OCX), ending a 16-year, multibillion-dollar effort to deliver a command and control system for GPS satellites; the decision was made by defense acquisition executive Michael Duffey on April 17.
The OCX contract was awarded to Raytheon (now RTX) in 2010 with a timetable for completion in 2016 at $3.7 billion; budget projections grew to nearly $8 billion — more than double the original cost.

RTX delivered the system to the Space Force in 2025, but further integrated tests revealed it was still not ready; problems were discovered 'across a broad range of capability areas that would put current GPS capabilities at risk.'
As of January 2026, costs were estimated at $6.27 billion; the Space Force will instead continue enhancing the existing Architecture Evolution Plan (AEP) control system.

stories.headline: Trump Says DOD Deal With Anthropic 'Possible' After White House Meeting With Amodei

key_facts.fact: President Trump told CNBC on April 21 that 'it's possible' a deal will be made to allow Anthropic to resume contracting with the Department of Defense, describing last week's White House meeting as 'very good talks.'

The statement follows Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's meeting last Friday with White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, described by both sides as 'productive and constructive.'

The reversal is striking: weeks ago the Trump administration had declared Anthropic a supply chain risk — a designation reserved for foreign adversaries — and Trump said the administration would 'not do business with them again.'

Anthropic's Mythos AI cybersecurity capability is what changed the calculus — civilian agencies and intelligence agencies want access to Mythos's vulnerability-discovery capabilities and are unwilling to be locked out by the Pentagon dispute.

stories.headline: UK Moves to Break Gas-Electricity Price Link, Raises Generator Levy to 55%

key_facts.fact: The UK government announced measures to decouple electricity prices from volatile gas prices, offering voluntary long-term fixed contracts to existing low-carbon generators covering about a third of Britain's power supply.
The Electricity Generator Levy rate was raised from 45% to 55% to tax excess profits when gas prices spike, ensuring more windfall revenue reaches households affected by the Iran war energy crisis.

Gas currently sets the wholesale price of electricity about 60% of the time in Britain, down from 90% in the early 2020s; the government projects this will fall to about 30% by the early 2030s through its clean energy mission.
The government is also exploring use of public land to unlock up to 10 GW of renewable capacity, and plans to accelerate 57,000 solar installations for households this year.

organizations: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

stories.headline: Nvidia PCB Supplier Victory Giant Surges ~60% in $2.2B Hong Kong IPO Debut

key_facts.fact: Victory Giant Technology Huizhou shares rocketed 59.6% in early trade to HK$335, having priced its IPO at HK$209.88 and raising HK$17.3 billion (~US$2.2 billion).
The IPO is Hong Kong's largest this year, surpassing debuts from Chinese AI startups Zhipu AI, MiniMax, and chip firms Biren Technology and OmniVision.
Victory Giant makes high-end printed circuit boards (PCBs), a crucial component of AI servers, with Nvidia as one of its key customers. The company is already listed in Shenzhen.
The company will use most IPO proceeds to expand production in mainland China as Beijing accelerates efforts to boost domestic semiconductor-adjacent manufacturing.
Pepperstone strategist Dilin Wu noted that tight supply in high-end PCB manufacturing benefits companies like Victory Giant, which gain from both policy support and financing accessibility.

stories.headline: Fed Chair Nominee Kevin Warsh Pledges Independence at High-Stakes Senate Hearing

key_facts.fact: Kevin Warsh, Trump's nominee to lead the Federal Reserve, told the Senate Banking Committee he is 'committed to ensuring that the conduct of monetary policy remains strictly independent' in prepared remarks released April 20.

Warsh qualified his independence pledge, saying Fed independence is 'at its peak in the operational conduct of monetary policy' but does not extend to the same 'special deference' in bank regulation, public monies, or international finance.

Republican Sen. Thom Tillis is effectively blocking a committee vote on Warsh until the DOJ drops its criminal investigation into Fed Chair Jerome Powell over a building renovation; Powell's term as chair ends May 15.
Warsh would be the wealthiest Fed chair if confirmed, with financial holdings totaling more than $100 million; Democrats signaled they will press him on transparency around those holdings.

The Fed funds rate currently sits at 3.50%-3.75% after the FOMC held steady at its last two meetings; Goldman Sachs expects up to two 25bp rate cuts in 2026 but timing remains uncertain due to Iran war-driven inflation.

stories.headline: Wärtsilä Wins 412 MW Gas Engine Order for Off-Grid Ohio Hyperscale Data Center

key_facts.fact: Wärtsilä received an order to supply 412 MW of gas engine power for a major hyperscale data center in Ohio, using 40 Wärtsilä 34SG spark-ignited gas engines.
The order brings Wärtsilä's total engine capacity sold into the US data center market to over 1.6 GW; this is the company's fourth US data center order.
The power plant will operate off-grid as primary power, enabling the data center to avoid long grid interconnection delays common to the US market, with commercial operation expected by early 2028.
This is the first deployment of Wärtsilä's proven 34SG engine model in a data center application; the modular design scales up to 500MW+.
